complaints.address: Complaints, Penrose, Queen Square, Bristol BS1 4QS
steps: Tell us by email, letter or phone; we'll confirm we have it within three working days.
A director who wasn't involved looks into it and writes to you with our answer.
If you're not happy with our answer, or eight weeks pass without one, you can ask the Financial Ombudsman Service to look at it.

independence.line: Restricted advice: we recommend pensions and investments from a panel of providers.
independence.restrictedTo: pensions and investments from a panel of six providers
body: We give restricted advice: we recommend from a panel of providers we've chosen, not the whole market.
We tell you which providers are on the panel before you decide.

check.title: Check it's us
check.intro: Fraudsters copy advisers' names and websites. Here's how to tell a real call or email from us.
never: We will never ask you to move money to a new account by phone or email.
We will never ask for your passwords or a card PIN.
We will never press you to decide on the day.
check.callback: If in doubt, hang up and call us back on the office number above, from another phone if you can.

fees.intro: What you pay us, in pounds, before you agree to anything. Our fees are a share of the money we advise on, with a minimum.
includes: A written recommendation, explained in a meeting
A review each year, and whenever your life changes
fees.paid: You can pay the initial fee directly, or from the money invested. The ongoing fee is taken monthly from your account, and you can stop it at any time.
fees.vat: Advice on investments and pensions isn't usually charged VAT. If a piece of work is, we tell you before we start.
fees.other: Platform and fund charges are separate, and you see them in pounds before you decide.

extras.label: A one-off review of a single pension

where: At our office on Queen Square

bring: Your will, if you have one
meeting.after: If you'd like to go ahead, we write to you with what we'd do and what it costs, in pounds. Nothing happens until you agree.

year.intro: What happens through the year once you're a client, so nothing comes as a surprise.

steps.when: Each year, in the month you choose
steps.what: Your review meeting: what's changed, and whether the plan still fits.
We send your figures and the questions we'll ask.
A written summary of what we agreed, and the fees you paid that year, in pounds.
A reminder about this tax year's allowances, if they apply to you.

year.adviserLeaves: If your adviser leaves, we introduce your new adviser in person before your next review.

questions.a: No. The first hour is free, and you leave with our fees in writing.

questions.q: Do I have to decide anything at the meeting?
questions.a: No. We write to you afterwards, and nothing happens until you agree.
1.5% of the money we advise on to begin, at least £1,500, then 0.75% each year. Platform and fund charges are separate.

questions.q: Can I stop the ongoing fee?
questions.a: Yes, at any time. The ongoing service stops with it.

questions.q: How do I know you're regulated?
questions.a: Search for our firm reference number on the FCA's Financial Services Register; the link is at the foot of every page.

advice.who: We usually work with people who have £100,000 or more in pensions and savings, or a decision of similar size.
advice.minimum: There's no minimum for a first meeting.
